original.target_description: Study 1, 17-country laboratory sample; effect of news negativity on normalized skin conductance (nSCL), second-by-second panel models underlying Figure 2. Original p. 3 (18890).

n.location: Cross-National Physiological Responses to News, sample paragraph
n.quote: Our results are based on 1,156 respondents
n.sample_role: Overall respondent sample; target-model analytic participant count not established.
n.exclusions: Target-model exclusions not established from main text.

es.quote: The shift shown in Fig. 2 is equivalent to 65% of the observed SD in nSCL.
es.metric: shift as percentage of observed SD in nSCL

p.quote: The evidence supports the expectation that physiological arousal is greater for negative news coverage than for positive news coverage.

replication.target_description: Study 1, Netherlands laboratory replication; H1 negativity predictor of normalized skin conductance in preregistered fixed-effects within-panel model, controlling logged time, negativity-by-time, lagged nSCL and story order. Supplied p. 5 describes preprocessing; results pp. 6–8.

n.quote: Participants (97 included in the analyses after preprocessing) saw four videos
n.sample_role: Analytic participants for H1 nSCL; Table 1 reports 40,346 second-level observations.
n.exclusions: Seven excluded from skin-conductance analysis: three non-response, one under-responsiveness, three wrong synchronisation (p. 5).

es.location: p. 7, Section 3.1; Table 1, p. 8, Negativity row / Replication column
es.quote: positive but not statistically significant effect of negativity on SCLs (𝛽 = 0.019, 𝑡 = 0.984, 𝑝 = 0.325)

p.quote: positive but not statistically significant effect of negativity on SCLs (𝛽 = 0.019, 𝑡 = 0.984, 𝑝 = 0.325)

reported_success.quote: To summarise, our study failed to replicate the statistical significance of the effect reported by SFN.

notes: The neutral description includes negative affect, but the original-to-replication shared target is physiological arousal (nSCL, H1); corrugator negative affect and self-reports are replication extensions. Original Figure 2 prints a standardized shift, not r; no conversion performed. Replication beta is printed rather than converted to requested r. Original main text does not print a p value for the Figure 2 shift. Authors report suggestive evidence elsewhere and discuss equivalence-test bounds; reported_success follows their explicit verdict for the preregistered significance test.
